s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive enlargement and discomfort of a digit with associated neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Enlargement of the left middle finger since birth
Limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
key_facts: The patient is a 14-year-old girl
The left middle finger has been enlarged since birth
The enlargement has been progressive
The patient developed tingling at the fingertip 3 months before presentation
There is limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
There is no history of trauma
There is no history of fever, weight loss, or appetite change
The overlying skin is normal
There is tenderness throughout the enlargement
Sensation is decreased distally
Resistance to flexion prevents full finger flexion
Laboratory studies are unremarkable
A CT scan of the hand shows overgrowth of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges plus surrounding soft tissue

shortlist.label: Macrodactyly
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive enlargement of the digit since birth

shortlist.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan shows overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue, suggesting a lipomatous process

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to lipofibromatous hamartoma, with possible involvement of the nerve

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible explanation for the progressive enlargement and associated neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Possible explanation for the neurological symptoms and progressive enlargement, although less likely given the absence of other characteristic features

raw.rationale: The patient's condition is characterized by progressive enlargement of the left middle finger since birth, which is a key feature of macrodactyly. The CT scan showing overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Although the CT scan suggests a lipomatous process, lipofibromatous hamartoma is a less common condition and the clinical presentation does not specifically suggest a hamartoma.

rejected.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Similar to lipofibromatous hamartoma, fibrolipomatous hamartoma is a less common condition and the clinical presentation does not specifically suggest a hamartoma.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically involves multiple limbs and is associated with port-wine stains, varicose veins, and other systemic features, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
rejected.why: There is no mention of café-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, or other characteristic features of neurofibromatosis type 1 in the patient's presentation.
